body:
## Why
A background worker has nobody to answer a permission prompt: attempt 2 of #3 sat status=waiting on a shell command outside the allowlist until the dispatcher (wrongly, now fixed) killed it. The widened allowlist reduces the frequency, but any residual prompt still strands a worker until max_runtime.

## What
- Ship a PreToolUse hook (gated on KB_TASK, like the Stop hook) that turns any would-be permission prompt into a structured deny: decision "deny" with a reason naming the allowlist and suggesting the closest allowed alternative. The model adapts instead of hanging.
- `hkb init` installs it next to the Stop hook; board.json gets `dispatch.on_unlisted_tool: "deny" | "prompt"` (default deny) so an attended board can keep prompts and answer them via `claude attach`.
- `hkb doctor` warns when the hook is missing while a claude-bg profile exists.
- Document in the profile section: attended = prompts + attach; unattended = deny.

## Done when
A worker that calls a non-allowlisted command gets an immediate deny message, keeps working, and never shows status=waiting for more than a heartbeat.
title: Permission story for unattended workers: auto-deny with a message instead of prompting
